title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.
card_summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.

sections.technical:
The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-112900.

email_summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. Tracked as CVE-2026-112900. Severity is rated critical.

title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated.
card_summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated.

sections.technical:
Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-111497.

email_summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Tracked as CVE-2026-111497. Severity is rated high.

title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
summary: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22.
card_summary: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22.
email_summary: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22. The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one.

title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
summary: Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.
card_summary: Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.

sections.impact:
The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.
